h1: No hot water from an unvented cylinder
title: No hot water from an unvented cylinder | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand no hot water from an unvented cylinder. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: First distinguish water that flows cold from no water flow. These point to different heating and supply investigations.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: If water runs normally but stays cold, the heating source, programme, immersion or temperature-control path may need assessment. If no water runs, the incoming supply, inlet controls or outlet path requires a different check.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Record whether all hot outlets are affected, whether cold taps work and whether normal heating controls were set to provide hot water. Do not dismantle an inlet valve or open electrical covers.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can a no-hot-water symptom mean two different types of fault?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cold flowing water suggests a heating problem; no flow suggests a supply or outlet problem. Describe which occurs.
